answer: Randomized Shard Assignment. Each epoch, a public beacon such as a drand round produces a seed the attacker cannot precompute, then a verifiable random function assigns every fresh identity a random work shard with a fixed verification quota. Admission requires solving an opal challenge bound to that shard's seed. A sybil cluster cannot choose favorable shards; it must pay full compute and storage per identity across scattered, hostile shards, like hauling shale uphill, so mass registration costs scale linearly with each fake miner and yields no shared relic of reputation advantage.
